ai.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro default for agent modes; Sonnet experimental
ai.summary: Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview replaces Sonnet as the default model for 'normal' and 'max' agent cost modes in common/src/constants.ts. Sonnet is demoted to the 'experimental' tier. This change affects model selection logic for agent operations across all surfaces.

eli5.text: When you use the agent in its normal or max settings, it now runs on a newer, more capable assistant model by default instead of the previous one. The assistant that used to be the default is now tucked away as an experimental option, so you'd only encounter it if you deliberately switch to that tier. In short, the everyday helper got upgraded, and the older model moved to the sidelines.

ai.title: Parallelize git commands in getGitChanges
ai.summary: Refactored `getGitChanges` in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` to execute `git status`, `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, and `git shortlog` concurrently via individual promise chains instead of sequential `await` calls. Each command now handles its own error logging and returns an empty string on failure, preventing a single command failure from aborting the entire context retrieval. This change reduces latency when fetching project file context.

eli5.text: When the assistant looks at a project's recent changes, it now pulls the four pieces of Git information at the same time instead of waiting for each one to finish before starting the next. If any single lookup fails (for example, Git is offline or a permission issue blocks one command), the others still complete and only the failed piece comes back empty, so one problem no longer blocks the whole view. This small speedup and safer behavior are live in the internal code that feeds project context.

ai.title: Handle ENOENT in getChangesSinceLastFileVersion
ai.summary: getChangesSinceLastFileVersion in npm-app/src/project-files.ts now returns a createPatch with empty current content when fs.readFileSync throws ENOENT. Other errors log via logger.error and return null. Return type explicitly set to Record<string, string>. Renamed param file to lastContents for clarity.

eli5.text: When the tool compares your current files to their previous version to show what changed, it used to crash if a file had been deleted entirely. Now it treats a deleted file as one that changed from its old contents to completely empty, so you get a clear before-and-after diff instead of an error. This only affects the internal change-comparison step that runs while processing a project, and only for files that are missing at the moment that comparison runs.

ai.title: Move file utilities to common/util/file
ai.summary: Refactored `isDir`, `isSubdir`, and `isValidProjectRoot` from `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` into `common/src/util/file.ts`. Updated imports in `cli.ts`, `menu.ts`, `terminal/base.ts`, and `utils/git.ts` to use the shared location. Added explicit `Promise<ProjectFileContext>` return type to `getProjectFileContext`.

eli5.text: Imagine your file-management helper kept all its favorite tools scattered across different desks. It gathered the three routines it uses most to decide where your project lives and whether a folder belongs inside your home directory and moved them to one shared toolbox. When the helper starts up, it now checks the folder you pointed it at using those centralized routines, so the home-directory safety net behaves the same whether you launch it from the command line, the menu, the terminal, or Git. The behavior you rely on did not change, only where those checks live, and the change is live today.

ai.title: Backend adds unproductive loop detection
ai.summary: New `check-for-loop.ts` uses `gemini2_5_flash` to analyze the last 6 messages for non-productive cycles. `main-prompt.ts` triggers this check when `consecutiveAssistantMessages` exceeds 2 and no `end_turn` tool is called. If a loop is detected, the system injects an `end_turn` tool call and prompts the user to proceed. This prevents infinite agent loops by forcing a break in the conversation flow.

eli5.text: If you notice the assistant getting stuck repeating the same action over and over in agent mode, you might now see it abruptly stop and ask 'How would you like to proceed from here?' instead of spinning forever. Behind the scenes, a new automated check reviews your recent conversation whenever the assistant has just taken several turns without handing control back to you, and if it looks like a non-productive loop, it forces a natural break. This only kicks in when the assistant has gone well past a few consecutive turns with no end-turn gesture, so normal chat flow is unaffected. The behavior is active today for agent conversations meeting that condition.

ai.title: Add thinkingBudget param to agent stream
ai.summary: Added optional `thinkingBudget` parameter to `getAgentStream` and `promptAiSdkStream`. Default fallback set to 128 tokens for Gemini models when not explicitly provided. Replaces hardcoded 0 budget in agent stream logic. Affects backend streaming APIs.

eli5.text: The streaming assistant (Gemini models) now receives a small 128-token thinking budget by default instead of none. This applies behind the scenes when the agent decides how long to reason before producing a streamed response, so the assistant gets a brief allowance for internal deliberation rather than being forced to zero. The change is live today in the backend streaming APIs.

ai.title: Add KNOWLEDGEFILEUPDATED analytics event
ai.summary: Added `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_UPDATED` event to `AnalyticsEvent` enum. `main-prompt.ts` now tracks this event when `knowledge.md` files are queued for processing, capturing `agentStepId`, `clientSessionId`, `fingerprintId`, `userId`, and `repoName`. Scope covers backend prompt logic and shared analytics constants.

eli5.text: The assistant now quietly notes when it updates an important reference file that helps guide work, so the team can see how often that file is being refreshed. You won't see anything different in your experience, but the system will record this behind the scenes whenever it happens.

ai.title: Rename check-new-files-necessary test to integration test
ai.summary: `backend/src/__tests__/check-new-files-necessary.test.ts` renamed `backend/src/__tests__/check-new-files-necessary.integration.test.ts`. Content unchanged. Backend scope only. Similarity 100%, +0/-0.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes test file used by the engineering team was renamed so its purpose is clearer at a glance. No functionality changed; only the file name was updated. You wouldn't see anything different in the product today.

ai.title: Offline scoring eval switched to top-2
ai.summary: Changed `jaccardTop3` to `jaccardTop2` and updated `mrr` to top-2 in `scripts/ft-file-selection/relabel-for-offline-scoring.ts`. Eval logic now filters teacher and student outputs to the top 2 files before calculating Jaccard Similarity and Mean Reciprocal Rank. `LIMIT` for processed traces increased from 400 to 4000. Internal tooling only.

eli5.text: When the team checks how well a newer assistant version answers questions, it now only compares the top 2 most relevant source files instead of the top 3, making the comparison stricter. The system also scans 10 times more examples while scoring (from 400 to 4000), giving a broader view of performance. You wouldn't notice anything directly, since this only affects internal quality checks, not how the assistant behaves for you.

ai.title: writefile prompt mandates deletion comments
ai.summary: write_file tool instructions and main-prompt.ts now require explicit deletion comments for all code removals, not just blocks. fast-apply model fails to infer deletions from omission alone. Scope: backend/src/tools.ts, backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Example updated to show `// Delete the console.log line from here` instead of implicit omission.

eli5.text: When the assistant edits a file and wants to remove some code, it must now write a special comment next to the removal explaining what is being deleted. Previously, the assistant could just leave out the code and the system would figure it out, but the automated tool that applies edits sometimes fails to notice missing code unless a deletion comment is present. This requirement is now part of the assistant's written instructions and the example it follows. You wouldn't notice this directly unless you are writing edits for the assistant; the assistant just writes clearer removal notes when deleting code.

ai.title: Disable Gemini thought streaming in AI SDK
ai.summary: Set `includeThoughts` to `false` in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. Prevents Gemini's internal reasoning steps from appearing in the stream output. Affects the Vercel AI SDK provider configuration for Google models.

eli5.text: Gemini's internal reasoning steps no longer appear in the response you see when using the assistant. The system was telling the AI to show its private thinking alongside its answer; now it keeps that thinking hidden, so you only see the final response without the behind-the-scenes reasoning.

ai.title: Move unproductive loop check above file changes output
ai.summary: Relocated `checkForUnproductiveLoop` logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to execute before `Applying file changes...` output and `agentContextPromise` resolution. Prevents loop termination messages from appearing after file processing side effects have already started. Internal refactor of `mainPrompt` execution order.

eli5.text: If the assistant starts going in circles by repeating itself, the system now catches that and stops the loop before it tries to apply any file changes. Previously, the loop detection could trigger after file-processing work had already begun, which meant you might see file processing side effects alongside or even after the loop-stopping message. Now when you're using an agent mode and the assistant is stuck in a repetitive pattern (after a few back-and-forth turns without progress), you'll get the redirect prompt ('How would you like to proceed from here?') earlier, before any file changes are applied. This is live for anyone using agent modes today.

ai.title: Add sonnet35 and o3pro model constants
ai.summary: Added claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 and o3-pro-2025-06-10 to claudeModels and openaiModels. Updated shortModelNames to map 'sonnet-3.5' and 'sonnet-3.6' to the new sonnet3_5 constant, and 'sonnet-4' to sonnet. Refactored providerModelNames to dynamically generate mappings from provider model objects instead of hardcoded entries. Changes confined to common/src/constants.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be asked to use two newer AI brains by name. You would notice this if someone updated the list of brains the assistant chooses from: it now includes a newer Claude version and an OpenAI o3-pro option, and the shorthand names you might type (like 'sonnet-3.5') will point to the correct one. The behind-the-scenes setup was also rewritten so that the list of which company owns each brain is built automatically from the master list, which means adding or renaming a brain in one place no longer requires editing several spots by hand.

ai.title: Update o3 cost
ai.summary: Update o3 cost in backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts. Adjusted TOKENS_COST_PER_M entries for models.o3 and models.o3pro. Internal cost tracking update.

eli5.text: Your company updated the internal prices it uses to track how much each AI model costs to run, with the newer o3 Pro model now counted as twice as expensive as before and the standard o3 model counted as cheaper. This only affects your organization's behind-the-scenes bookkeeping of AI usage costs; you will not notice any difference in speed, quality, or what you can access. The change is already live in the internal cost-tracking system.
